english: Let $R(x)=\alpha x^{2}+\beta x+\gamma$ be the remainder when the polynomial $x^{6}$ is divided by $(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)$. Then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि बहुपद $x^{6}$ को $(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)$ से भाग देने पर शेषफल $R(x)=\alpha x^{2}+\beta x+\gamma$ है। तब $\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: By the division algorithm $x^{6}=(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)Q(x)+R(x)$ with $\deg R\le2$.
Putting $x=1,2,3$ (the remainder theorem for each linear factor) gives $R(1)=1$, $R(2)=2^{6}=64$, $R(3)=3^{6}=729$.
Replace the first column by the constants: $\Delta_\alpha=\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\64&2&1\\729&3&1\end{vmatrix}=1(2-3)-1(64-729)+1(192-1458)=-1+665-1266=-602$.
Check: $\alpha$ is the second divided difference $\dfrac{729-2\cdot64+1}{2}=\dfrac{602}{2}=301$; the full remainder is $301x^{2}-840x+540$, and $R(2)=1204-1680+540=64$.
originality_note: New combination: the remainder on division by a cubic with three known roots is found through three remainder-theorem values and one Cramer quotient, without long division (way 5). Closest known: remainder of a polynomial on division by (x-a)(x-b), found from two values. Different because: three nodes give a 3x3 system, and only one coefficient is asked, which Cramer's rule gives directly.

concept_use.Cramer's rule: alpha = Delta_alpha / Delta from the 3x3 system for the coefficients of R.
The remainder theorem gives R(1) = 1, R(2) = 64, R(3) = 729, the right-hand sides of the system.

stem_review: Read as a student: the divisor is a cubic with distinct roots, so the remainder has degree at most 2 and is unique; alpha is its x^2-coefficient. Checked with sympy: remainder 301x^2 - 840x + 540. Answer 301, a positive 3-digit integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Remainder theorem at 1, 2, 3 gives a 3x3 system; Cramer gives alpha.
justification: Routine chain: three substitutions, two determinants; no insight beyond setting up the system. Comparable to 2024-P1-Q8 (L2) in demand.
